5. The defendant nos. 1-6 filing written statement contested in the suit. The case of the defendants are that the suit is not maintainable in its present from and the suit is bad for non-joinder of parties etcetera. The further case of the defendants are that Jitu Prang being the owner and the possessor of the partible land had died leaving only son Soleman, the predecessor of defendant nos. 1-6. Pachan, the another son of Jitu Prang died on 20.02.1961 as such, Ayesha Khatun Bibi, the daughter of pre-deceased son of Jitu Prang did not inherit any land as heirs of Jitu Prang in to the partible land. Although Ayesha Khatun Bibi did not inherit any land into the property of her grandfather Jitu Prang but to serve the interest of humanity and mankind she was given some land amicably through the disputed deed of partition. But Ayesha Khatun Bibi could not be satisfied of the said portion rather she becoming greedy for more land filed the false suit which is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 20. On going to the judgment of the trial Court I find that the trial Court very meticulously scanned and considered the evidence on record in respect of the death of Jitu Prang and thereafter came to a conclusion that he died in the year 1961. There appears no misreading or non-reading or non-consideration of the evidence in respect of the death of Jitu Prang. The learned Advocate of the petitioner could not show the misreading on non reading or non consideration of the evidence on record in respect of the death of Jitu Prang. So, I find it difficult to differ with the concurrent findings of the Courts below in respect of the death of Jitu Prang.
